info.name: Dokkai API
info.description:
HTTP API for Dokkai — a graph-aware vector database over a codebase.

Every route except Health, Auth → Login and Auth → Status requires a bearer token (see the Auth folder). Auth cannot be disabled.

Usage order:
1. Auth → Login (default admin/admin on first boot; captures {{authToken}} automatically and applies it to every other request via the collection's bearer auth).
2. Config → Set LLM provider (or set OLLAMA_CHAT_MODEL on the server). Requires the admin role.
3. Instances → Start pipeline (captures {{jobId}} automatically).
4. Instances → Get job (poll until status = succeeded), or Job events (SSE) to stream progress.
5. Chat → Chat (SSE): note Postman shows the raw event stream. Requires the admin or user role.
6. Graph → List graphs / Get project graph / Get entity neighborhood / Get file dependency view, once a project is ingested.
7. Routines → Launch review run or Launch bug hunt run (captures {{runId}}/{{jobId}} automatically), then Get routine run to poll for findings/summary once status is done. Bug hunt requires an Ollama-resolved provider in this release (see its saved 400 example). Routines → Playbooks / Routines → Skills manage the reusable documents a run can attach: playbooks are pushed by name (at most 4); skills are pulled by the model itself from the full catalog every run (at most 3), never named at launch.

Roles: admin (everything, incl. user management and POST /config/llm), user (chat, ingestion, deletes, routine-run launch/delete, playbook/skill writes, all reads), viewer (read-only GETs only). A role that can't perform an action gets 403 "role '<role>' cannot perform this action".

Note: only one pipeline/refresh/graph/routine job may run per project at a time — a second one returns 409 (see the '409 - job already running' saved examples).

Collection variables let you avoid editing every request: set {{baseUrl}}, {{repoPath}}, {{projectName}} once.

request.description: Public. Authenticate and receive a 30-day bearer token. The test script saves the token into {{authToken}}, which the collection's bearer auth applies to every other request. default_admin_active is true while the seeded admin/admin credentials are unchanged.
Public. { enabled: true, default_admin_active } -- whether the seeded admin/admin credentials are still active.
Requires any authenticated role. Current user's username, role, session expiry, default_admin_active.
Requires the admin role. Never includes password hashes.
Requires the admin role. role is one of admin|user|viewer. The test script saves the new user's id into {{userId}}.
Requires the admin role. 400 if you try to delete your own user or the last remaining admin.
Requires any authenticated role. 401 if current_password doesn't match. Revokes every OTHER session for this user; the session making this request stays valid.
Requires any authenticated role. Invalidates the session (bearer token) used for this request.

Requires the admin or user role. Enqueue the ingestion pipeline. Returns { job_id, status } immediately and runs in the background.

Set recreate:true only once, to migrate the schema (it drops the whole collection). The test script saves job_id into {{jobId}}.

describe defaults to true. Set describe:false to opt out of per-entity LLM descriptions for this run -- this also skips the descriptor pre-flight below, and the summary named vector stays empty for this run's chunks.

Fail-loud descriptor policy (describe:true only): the configured DESC_MODEL/DESC_PROVIDER is checked before the job is created. Missing or unavailable descriptor -> 400, no job created (see the '400 - no descriptor model' saved example).

Per-project job lock: a second pipeline/refresh/graph-only job for a project that already has one queued/running -> 409, no job created (see the '409 - job already running' saved example).

response.name: 400 - no descriptor model

request.description: DANGER: recreate:true drops the ENTIRE collection (all projects) before inserting. Use only once, after a schema change.

describe:false opts out of per-entity LLM descriptions for this run. Skips the descriptor pre-flight (no 400 even if DESC_MODEL is unset/unpulled) and ingests without descriptions -- the summary named vector stays empty for this project's chunks (equivalent to `dokkai ingest --no-describe`).

Requires the admin or user role. Enqueue a graph-ONLY run (cgr only -- no chunking, no LLM descriptions, no embedding, no Weaviate). Returns { job_id, status } immediately; runs in the background with stages cgr -> done and kind: "graph". result.ingest.output_json is the same canonical graph JSON path (ingested/<project>.json) the full pipeline produces, readable by the Graph API as soon as the job succeeds. Shares the same per-project job lock as Start pipeline / Refresh descriptions. The test script saves job_id into {{jobId}}.
List all ingestion jobs, most recent first. In-memory; resets on server restart.

Poll a job's progress. Watch stage (cgr -> chunk -> describe -> upsert -> done for pipeline jobs, chunk -> describe -> update -> done for refresh jobs, cgr -> done for graph-only jobs), stage_progress {stage,done,total}, kind (pipeline|refresh|graph), and result.vectorize.descriptions (pipeline) or result.descriptions (refresh) -- graph-only jobs' result has only ingest.output_json.

Streams the job's progress as Server-Sent Events, mirroring Chat (SSE)'s framing. Emits the current state on connect, then again whenever updated_at changes (~0.5s poll). event: job for in-progress updates, event: done for the terminal state (status = succeeded|failed), after which the stream closes. Each event's data is the same Job object as GET /instances/jobs/{id}. Unknown job_id -> plain 404 (not a stream).

Note: Postman buffers the stream and shows it after completion; use curl -N for live events.

Requires the admin or user role. Re-run only the describe pass over an already-ingested project (background job; no cgr, no re-embedding of unchanged text). Cache is honored (default force:false) -- unchanged entities cost nothing. Same fail-loud descriptor pre-flight as the pipeline, plus 404 if the project has no chunks and 409 if its graph JSON is missing from ingested/. The test script saves job_id into {{jobId}}.

response.name: 404 - project has no chunks
409 - no graph JSON found

request.description:
Requires the admin or user role. Streams a Server-Sent Events response: sources → token* → done (or error). project_name must match an ingested repo. audience ∈ developer|manager|customer.

Each entry in the 'sources' event's data array includes both file_path (relative) and absolute_path (full path on disk, as persisted at ingest time).

Note: Postman buffers the stream and shows it after completion; use curl -N for live tokens.
Follow-up in the same conversation, using {{conversationId}} captured by the previous request.
List stored conversations (persisted in Postgres). Includes title (derived from the first user message, null for older conversations) and audience.
Full history (messages + their sources) for one conversation.
Requires the admin or user role. Delete a conversation and its history.

List every project with an ingested graph in ingested/. Includes chunks (Weaviate chunk count, null if Weaviate is unreachable) and repo_path (derived from a File node, null if underivable). Returns [] when nothing has been ingested yet. Restart-proof -- read straight off the filesystem.
Normalized graph for the project: code-entity nodes (Class/Function/Method/Interface/Enum/Type) and edges among them only. 404 if the project was never ingested.
Every node (code entities, folders, files, modules, packages, the project, external packages) and every edge, up to limit.

Resolved graph node for name (same resolution as the neighborhood endpoint's entity param), enriched with description and chunk_text fetched from Weaviate via the same deterministic-UUID lookup the MCP get_entity tool uses. description/chunk_text are null (not an error) when the entity has no chunk in Weaviate or Weaviate is unreachable. 404 if the project has no graph, or if the entity isn't in it.

BFS over CALLS/INHERITS/IMPLEMENTS/OVERRIDES/DEFINES/DEFINES_METHOD edges only (never IMPORTS or containment/external edges). Nodes carry hop (0 = center); the center is also returned separately. 404 if the project has no graph, or if entity isn't in it.
Directed file-to-file dependency aggregation, internal files only (external packages/modules excluded, self-loops skipped). Each edge has a total weight and a per relationship-type types breakdown.

Requires the admin or user role. Launches a code review run as a background job. Returns 202 { run_id, job_id } immediately. See also 'Launch bug hunt run' for kind: bughunt.

base_ref defaults to the project's default base branch (origin/HEAD, else local main/master) when omitted. model/provider (both optional) override the active LLM config for this run only. playbooks (optional, at most 4) pushes named playbooks into the prompt -- see the Playbooks folder.

Model resolution -- no hardcoded default: model/provider in the body, else the active POST /config/llm config; if neither resolves to a usable provider+model, 400 with the 'no LLM configured' message (see the saved example).

Pre-flights (in order, before any job is created): project must have an ingested graph (404), repo_path must be a git repo (400), base_ref/target_ref must resolve (400), every named playbook must exist and apply to kind: review (400), the resolved LLM must be healthy (400).

Shares the same per-project job lock as /instances/pipeline, /instances/graph and /instances/{project}/describe -- 409 if a job is already running for this project (see the '409 - job already running' saved example). The test script saves run_id into {{runId}} and job_id into {{jobId}}.

response.name: 400 - no LLM configured
404 - project not ingested

item.name: Launch review run (explicit base_ref + model override)

request.description: Same as Launch review run, but with an explicit base_ref and a per-run model/provider override -- these bypass the active POST /config/llm config for just this run. qwen2.5-coder:14b is the recommended local model for review (measured: 3b-class models are not reliable for review judgment).

Same as Launch review run, but pushes up to 4 named playbooks into the run's prompt (selection order = priority order). Each name must already exist and must apply to kind: review (a playbook's own routines field) -- validated synchronously at launch, see the 'Launch review run' -> '400 - playbook not found' saved example.

Requires the admin or user role. Launches a bug-hunt run -- a free-text scope investigated by a bounded (<=12-round) agentic tool loop over the WHOLE project (not a diff) -- as a background job. Returns 202 { run_id, job_id } immediately, same polling shape as a review run.

scope is required (422 if omitted, see the saved example). path_prefix is optional and restricts REPORTED findings to files under that repo-relative prefix; the agent may still read files elsewhere for context.

Ollama-native only in this release: if the resolved provider (launch payload or active config) isn't ollama, this 400s synchronously (see the '400 - non-Ollama provider' saved example) -- the exact same check the agent loop itself would raise.

Honest quality note: with qwen2.5-coder:14b, roughly half of read-verified findings can still misread the code they cite (e.g. calling an explicit try/catch 'no exception handling'). Verify findings against the evidence trail (tool calls made, cited entities, line anchors) before acting on them -- see the README's Bug hunt section. The test script saves run_id into {{runId}} and job_id into {{jobId}}.

response.name: 422 - scope missing
400 - non-Ollama provider

body.raw:
{
  "kind": "bughunt",
  "project": "{{projectName}}",
  "scope": "audit the auth module for privilege-escalation bugs",
  "provider": "openai",
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini"
}

item.name: Launch bug hunt run (with playbooks + model override)

body.raw:
{
  "kind": "bughunt",
  "project": "{{projectName}}",
  "scope": "audit the auth module for privilege-escalation bugs",
  "playbooks": ["{{playbookName}}"],
  "model": "qwen2.5-coder:14b",
  "provider": "ollama"
}

request.description: Same as Launch bug hunt run, but pushes up to 4 named playbooks (each must apply to kind: bughunt) and overrides the model/provider for just this run -- must still resolve to ollama, see 'Launch bug hunt run' -> '400 - non-Ollama provider'.

Requires any authenticated role. Most recent first, optionally filtered by project and/or kind (query params, both optional; limit defaults to 50, max 200). Each entry carries severity_counts (severity -> count over that run's findings).

Requires any authenticated role. The run's full detail, findings included. Poll this (or stream GET /instances/jobs/{{jobId}}/events) until status is done or failed; summary/stats/findings fill in once terminal.
Requires the admin or user role. Deletes the run, cascading to its findings (404 if the run doesn't exist).

Requires any authenticated role. Local branches of the project's repository (current branch and most-recently-committed first) plus the resolved default_base. 404 if the project has no ingested graph; 400 if repo_path isn't a git repo or no default base branch could be determined.
Requires any authenticated role. Lists playbooks -- omits content in favor of content_bytes; use Get playbook for the full content.

Requires the admin or user role. routines defaults to ["review", "bughunt"] (both) when omitted. content is markdown, up to 16KB, optional leading YAML frontmatter (stored/returned verbatim, not parsed). name must be non-empty, <=128 chars, no leading/trailing whitespace, and no '/', '\\', or control characters (it's a REST path segment).

response.name: 400 - name has a slash

request.description: Requires any authenticated role. A playbook's full detail, content included.
Requires the admin or user role. Updates content and/or routines -- fields left unset are left unchanged.
Requires the admin or user role.
Requires any authenticated role. Lists skills -- omits content in favor of content_bytes; use Get skill for the full content.

Requires the admin or user role. description is what a run's own model sees in the skills catalog when deciding whether to load this skill (keep it short and relevance-scoped) -- there is no launch-time field for skills, they are model-PULLED every run (contrast with playbooks, which are pushed by name). content is markdown, up to 16KB, optional leading YAML frontmatter.
Requires any authenticated role. A skill's full detail, content included.
Requires the admin or user role. Updates description and/or content -- fields left unset are left unchanged.
Requires the admin or user role.
Requires the admin role. Configure a local Ollama chat model. Validates that the model is installed.

Requires the admin role. Configure a remote provider: a built-in (openai, gemini, anthropic), an id registered via config/providers.json (see List providers), or any other id paired with base_url (an OpenAI-compatible endpoint). Requires provider_data.key for the built-ins; optional for a custom endpoint that doesn't need one. The exact model is probed at save time (models.retrieve) -- an invalid/retired model is rejected with 400 and nothing is saved.
Current active LLM configuration (404 if none set).

Provider ids the registry can serve directly: the built-ins (openai, gemini, anthropic) plus any id registered from config/providers.json. Excludes ollama (its own local-only path) and never returns a key or anything derived from one.

Models advertised by the active provider. Remote providers (openai/gemini/anthropic and any config/providers.json-registered or custom id) fetch the provider's live catalog and fall back to a static/declared list on any failure -- the anthropic-messages shape (anthropic) uses a short (5s) timeout for that call, the openai-completions shape (openai, gemini, everything else) uses the SDK's own default; ollama lists what's pulled locally.
Connectivity check for the active provider -- probes the currently configured model (not a hard-coded one): remote providers call models.retrieve(model), ollama checks /api/tags.
